description:
First slice of the consistency checker. Reads object storage with no running cluster and validates chunk structure.

Object storage has no manifest and no index -- the namespace is flat and self-describing by listing: c/{shard_tag}/{inverted_version_base36} for transaction chunks, s/{shard_tag}/... for Olivine snapshot bundles. So there is no referential-integrity check to make; validation is structural and per-shard.

Checks:
- Every key parses via Keys.extract_version/1, and key_to_version(basename) == header.max_version (the writer names a chunk for its last commit).
- Header: magic BDCH, format version, min_version <= max_version, directory_size == txn_count*16, min/max match first/last directory entries, data length >= max(offset+length).
- Directory ascending by version; every slice decodes as a valid BRDT transaction whose commit version matches its directory entry.
- Per shard, chunk version ranges must not overlap and must not have unexpected gaps. This is the highest-value check: ChunkReader.covering_chunk_keys/2 assumes the leading run of chunk names covers the target version, so an overlap or gap produces a SILENT replay gap rather than an error.

Note there are no checksums anywhere in the chunk encoding -- integrity rests on magic bytes plus structural completeness. LocalFilesystem.get_with_version/2 returns a sha256: content digest that is available for free.

Legal, do not report as faults: superseded or unreferenced chunks (never deleted by design, bedrock-wxf.6). Report but do not fault: .bedrock-tmp.* scratch debris (bedrock-ck3).

Reuse Chunk.decode/1, Chunk.decode_header/1, ChunkReader.list_chunk_metadata/2 (supports on_error: :skip) and Keys rather than reimplementing decode.

Shape: logic in a plain, unit-testable module under lib/bedrock/; lib/mix/tasks/bedrock.fsck.ex is a thin argv shell only, so the harness can call the checker in-process and get structured results instead of parsing stdout. Must run fully offline against a store path or MinIO URL. Follows the existing mix bedrock.dump_storage / mix bedrock.analyze_index convention.

comments.text:
Correction to this ticket's premise, established during implementation and verified independently.

I wrote that 'an overlap or gap produces a silent replay gap' in ChunkReader.covering_chunk_keys/2. The gap half was wrong. The implementation is:

    list_chunks()  # newest-first, keys are inverted versions
    |> Stream.take_while(&(max_version_from_key(&1) >= target_version))

That take_while is SOUND across gaps. It walks newest-to-oldest and stops at the first chunk whose named max is below the target, so every chunk that could hold the target is taken regardless of holes between them.

What actually breaks it:
- name/header disagreement -- max_version_from_key reads the NAME, so a chunk named lower than its header's true max gets cut by take_while even though it holds the target
- overlap -- a version replays twice, out of order

Both are faulted. Gaps are deliberately NOT faulted, and this is the right call: versions are sequencer commit versions rather than a dense sequence, a shard only receives transactions that touch it, and chunks carry no link to a predecessor. So nothing in the store distinguishes a lost chunk from a quiet shard. Gaps are reported as :version_gap notes in ShardResult.gaps for a caller that DOES know the expected stream -- e.g. a chaos harness driving a known workload, which is exactly bedrock-hve.5 onward. That is the right division of labour: fsck reports what it can prove, the harness judges what it has the context to judge.

Consistent with the 'guard only real hazards' convention -- a check that cannot distinguish a fault from normal operation is noise, not safety.

title: mix bedrock.fsck: offline structural validation of object-storage chunks
